calls.head: Like for like: Suter vs. Dach
calls.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Suter’s line (Kaskimäki, Suter and Stenberg) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Canadiens’ fourth line is Dach, Evans and Xhekaj.

STL.head: We leaned St. Louis’s way (57%), but Montréal had other ideas.

MTL.head: We had Montréal as slight underdogs (43%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: Jacob Fowler stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Fowler stopped all 46 shots, worth 4.0 expected goals. That is more than Montréal’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 500 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: St. Louis shut down Montréal’s power play
surprises.body: Montréal has a weaker power play than most. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: 1.1 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.1 (about 6.7 against St. Louis) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Fowler stops all 46 to blank the Blues
paras: Zachary Bolduc opened the scoring for the Canadiens midway through the second. Florian Xhekaj, in his ninth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Mike Matheson, early in the third to make it 2-0.

The Blues had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Blues win about six in ten. Jacob Fowler was the difference, stopping 46 of 46. Jordan Binnington stopped 18 of 20 for the Blues. Fowler has won six straight starts. The Canadiens moved to 7-3-2 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Blues dropped to 5-6-1, sixth in the Central.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Canadiens.
The Canadiens’ Josh Anderson played his 700th NHL game.
With Nick Suzuki out, Oliver Kapanen took his spot, though he won only 2 of 7 faceoffs.
